_meta.purpose: Real, cited regional food data for the Fit & Fed nutrition tracker. Replaces placeholder/mock food content for screen-designer and app-builder.
_meta.diasporaScope: A small set of Western/diaspora staples is included per research/product-research.md's diaspora persona (dual-cuisine users), not a full Western database.
_meta.unitConvention: Every food carries at least one householdPortion (the unit people actually serve/log in) mapped to a gram equivalent, plus macro/micronutrient values per 100g so the app can compute any portion from grams.

confidenceLegend.direct-fct: Value traced to a named national/regional food composition table (Nigerian FCT, WAFCT-covered Ghana staple, or Kenya FCT 2018), via a secondary compilation that itself cites that FCT.
confidenceLegend.usda: Value traced to USDA FoodData Central (directly for raw/simple ingredients, or via a USDA-sourced nutrition aggregator).
confidenceLegend.academic: Value traced to a peer-reviewed or government academic source analyzing the specific food.
confidenceLegend.compiled-estimate: No single authoritative figure exists for this composite dish; value is a reasoned point estimate within a documented range from multiple independently-prepared nutrition-tracking sources, flagged with the range and the reason for variance (usually oil/meat quantity in home recipes).

_meta.knownLimitation: This research pass used web search rather than direct binary/PDF access to the primary FAO/INFOODS WAFCT 2019, Nigerian FCT, and Kenya FCT 2018 documents (tool access to those PDFs was blocked in this environment). Values below are sourced from secondary compilations that explicitly cite those FCTs (e.g. FitNigerian, AfroTools, FitSavanna) or from USDA-derived aggregators for raw ingredients, not from reading the FCT line items directly. See docs/data-sourcing.md Limitations section before treating any single value as lab-analyzed-precise.

foods.name: Jollof Rice
foods.valueSpread: Independent trackers report 145-241 kcal/100g for jollof rice depending on oil quantity and tomato-stock ratio; this entry uses the lower, lighter-oil end reported by a Nigeria-specific tracker. A household cook using more oil will run materially higher; the app should treat this as a starting default, not a fixed truth.

source.name: FitNigerian — Jollof Rice Nutrition Facts
source.note: States it draws on Nigerian food-composition data; cross-checked against NutriScan, SnapCalorie, and AfroTools figures which range up to 241 kcal/100g.

source.name: FitNigerian — Garri (White) Nutrition Facts, citing the Nigerian Food Composition Table 2017

foods.name: Eba (cooked garri swallow)
foods.valueSpread: Reports range ~99-125 kcal/100g cooked; cooking water ratio (how loose/firm the swallow is made) is the main driver. 112 kcal is used as the midpoint.

source.name: BeHealthyAfrica — How Many Calories are in Gari/Eba?, and SnapCalorie Eba Nutrition (both derived from garri's dry-basis Nigerian FCT values adjusted for water absorption)

foods.name: Egusi Soup
foods.valueSpread: Re-checked against the cited source: NutriScan's own 250g-bowl figure is ~455 kcal, i.e. exactly 182 kcal/100g x 2.5 — the previous revision of this entry incorrectly stated a 350-400 kcal/250g range as 'consistent,' which was arithmetically false (455 is above that range) and has been corrected. Meat/fish/palm-oil content still varies substantially by household recipe: lean, minimal-oil versions run closer to 400-450 kcal/250g bowl (~160-180 kcal/100g), while palm-oil-heavy versions run 600+ kcal/250g bowl (~240+ kcal/100g). 182 kcal/100g sits at the lean-to-moderate end of that real spread. The macro panel was also rescaled in this pass so it Atwater-reconciles with the stated kcal (12.5P/7C/11.5F x 4/4/9 = ~182 kcal, vs. the previous 14.3/8/13.2 panel which computed to 208 kcal against a 182 kcal label).

source.name: NutriScan App — Egusi Soup: Calories, Nutrition and Health Benefits

foods.name: Pounded Yam
foods.valueSpread: Wide disagreement across sources (109-268 kcal/100g): fresh-pounded yam (high moisture, traditional mortar-and-pestle prep) sits at the low end used here; reconstituted yam-flour ('poundo yam') products run much higher (drier basis), which the app should model as a separate ingredient rather than conflating with fresh pounded yam.

source.name: FitNigerian — Pounded Yam Nutrition Facts & Value

foods.name: Suya (grilled spiced beef skewer, yaji spice)
foods.valueSpread: Beef vs. chicken suya and yaji (peanut/spice marinade) quantity shift fat and carb values; iron/zinc are qualitatively reported as notable (suya is grilled red meat plus ground peanuts) but no source gave exact mg figures, so those fields are left null rather than invented.

source.name: Calorique — Calories in Suya: Nutrition Facts, Ingredients & Variations

foods.name: Ogbono Soup
foods.valueSpread: Derived by dividing a recorded 250g-serving figure (350 kcal, 10g protein, 25g fat, 15g carb) by 2.5; pure ogbono seed itself is far denser (499 kcal/100g) — the soup figure assumes a typical dilution with broth, meat/fish, and vegetables. Household recipes vary.

source.name: Low Carb Africa — Ogbono Soup (Draw Soup) recipe nutrition panel
FitNigerian — Fried Plantain/Dodo Nutrition Facts & Value

foods.name: Waakye (rice and beans cooked with sorghum leaves/millet stalks)
foods.valueSpread: Independent trackers show roughly 167-194 kcal/100g for cooked waakye depending on rice:beans ratio, oil quantity, and whether stew/accompaniments are folded into the tracked entry; packaged/commercial waakye products and accompaniment-inclusive meals run higher still. 167 kcal/100g is used here and is corroborated by a second, independently-listed serving entry (379.1 kcal per 227g serving on a USDA-linked database, which is ~167 kcal/100g) — i.e. two independent sources converge on this figure at the bean/rice-only (no heavy accompaniments) end of the range.

source.name: Ayo/MyNetDiary — Waakye Beans & Rice Nutrition Facts

foods.name: Banku (fermented corn and cassava dough)
foods.valueSpread: Only an energy figure was corroborated across sources; a full macro breakdown was not found with confidence, so protein/carbs/fat are left null rather than invented. Flagged as a coverage gap.

source.name: SnapCalorie — Banku Nutrition

foods.name: Fufu (cassava and plantain, pounded)
foods.valueSpread: Fufu's calorie density varies substantially by base starch and preparation: cassava-heavy or flour-reconstituted fufu runs denser (up to roughly 250-300+ kcal/100g), while plantain-forward, freshly-pounded fufu runs lower (as low as ~150 kcal/100g, reflecting more fiber/water). 166 kcal/100g is used here for a mixed cassava-and-plantain, freshly-pounded preparation (the most commonly logged household form), and is corroborated across NutriScan and general fufu-nutrition guides that converge in the ~150-170 kcal/100g band for that preparation style specifically.

source.name: NutriScan App — Fufu: Calories, Nutrition and Health Benefits

foods.name: Kenkey (fermented, steamed corn dough)
foods.valueSpread: Sources disagree substantially (112-180 kcal/100g) depending on Ga vs. Fante preparation and fermentation time; 140 kcal is a rough midpoint, not a lab value.

source.name: SnapCalorie — Kenkey Nutrition (cross-checked against multiple kenkey trackers)

foods.name: Groundnut Soup / Nkatenkwan (peanut soup)
foods.valueSpread: Very wide range across recorded recipes (92-273 kcal/100g equivalent) depending on whether meat/chicken is included and how much raw groundnut paste is used. A peer-reviewed University of Ghana study on the proximate composition of Ghanaian composite soups exists (see source) but its exact reported figures were not extractable in this pass; this is a compiled midpoint, explicitly low-confidence, and a strong candidate for the nutrition-analyst review flagged in docs/data-sourcing.md.

source.name: Records, Sarpong et al. — Proximate composition and serving sizes of selected composite Ghanaian soups (University of Ghana)
Kenya Food Composition Tables 2018 (via secondary compilation)
source.note: Value corroborated via myfooddata.com's Kenyan-ugali entry and caloriehealthy.com, both of which attribute figures to KFCT 2018.

foods.name: Sukuma Wiki (stir-fried collard greens/kale)
foods.valueSpread: Steamed-without-oil preparation runs far lower (~25 kcal/100g); the stir-fried figure used here reflects typical household prep with oil/onion/tomato.

source.name: Fit Savanna — Sukuma Wiki (Stir-Fried Kales), citing Kenya Food Composition Tables 2018

foods.name: Githeri (boiled maize and beans)
foods.valueSpread: Fat content (7.6g/100g) is high relative to a plain maize-and-beans dish, implying most recorded recipes include added cooking oil; a plain-boiled version would run lower-fat. Reported as found rather than adjusted.

source.name: NutrInformation — Nutritional Composition of Githeri

foods.name: Chapati (wheat flatbread)
foods.valueSpread: Per-piece figures (~120 kcal for a 40g chapati) scale to ~300 kcal/100g; oil/ghee brushed on the surface after cooking adds ~40-45 kcal per teaspoon on top of this base and is common in Kenyan households, so real-world values run higher.

source.name: AceBlend — Chapati Calories: The Complete Nutritional Guide

foods.name: Nyama Choma (roasted goat meat)
foods.valueSpread: Fried/extra-fatty cuts run to ~153 kcal/100g; protein/fat split here is a reasoned estimate based on typical roasted-goat composition since the found sources gave energy but not a full consistent macro panel.

source.name: RecipeOfHealth — Nyama Choma (Roast Meat) nutrition panel

foods.name: Mandazi (fried sweet dough)
foods.valueSpread: Corrected in this pass: the previous revision cited '292-320 kcal per piece' for the same 60g piece used here, which contradicted 320 kcal/100g x 60g = 192 kcal/piece (a 292-320 kcal piece at 320 kcal/100g would need to weigh ~90-100g, not 60g). Re-checking the sources: 292-320 kcal/100g is actually the range independent trackers report on a per-100g basis (not per-piece) for fried mandazi, depending on coconut milk/egg content and oil absorption; 320 kcal/100g is the upper-middle of that range and is independently corroborated by a small-piece source reporting 99 kcal for a 31g piece (≈318 kcal/100g when scaled). Piece weight itself varies widely by vendor/household from a small ~31g piece (~99 kcal) to the 60g piece used as this entry's default household portion (320 kcal/100g x 60g = 192 kcal/piece). The previously-cited '~28 kcal/piece vegan mahamri' figure has been removed: a fried-dough piece at 28 kcal is not physically plausible (it was an uncaught source artifact, likely a per-gram or per-small-bite figure misread as per-piece) and no source in this pass gave a corroborated numeric value for the vegan mahamri variant, so it is left out entirely rather than assigned an invented number; it should be added as its own catalog item with its own sourcing pass if/when tracked.

source.name: Calorique — Mandazi Calories, cross-checked against a Nutritionix small-piece (31g) mandazi entry

foods.name: Managu (African nightshade, boiled)
foods.valueSpread: Fresh-leaf iron is reported at 1.0mg/100g vs. 6.2mg/100g once boiled/concentrated; the boiled (as-eaten) figure is used since that is how the food is logged.

source.name: Nutrition Point Kenya — Indigenous Vegetables Eaten in Kenya

foods.name: Terere (amaranth leaves, cooked)
foods.valueSpread: Iron reported qualitatively as '~29% of DRI' rather than an absolute mg figure by the source used; left null rather than back-calculated from an assumed DRI baseline.

source.name: Nutrition-and-You.com — Amaranth Greens Nutrition Facts and Health Benefits (cross-checked against USDA-derived nutritionvalue.org entry for raw amaranth leaves)
